faqs.q: Will the fleece pill after multiple washes, and how do I pick between cotton, polyester, or blend?
faqs.a: Material pick depends on your decoration goal: 100% polyester for full-color dye sublimation (graphics built into the fabric, no print layer to crack or peel); 100% cotton for screen printing (best ink adhesion and the classic soft-cotton hand-feel); cotton-polyester blend for tackle twill and embroidery (durable base for stitched-on letters and numbers). Our fleece is brushed and pre-shrunk to minimize pilling — wash inside-out cold, tumble dry low, and skip fabric softener for the longest life. Polyester pills less than cotton over time, but proper care extends the life of any fabric choice.

faqs.q: How does sublimation handle frequent practice washing?
faqs.a: Sublimation bonds the design directly into the polyester fibers, so there is no print layer to crack or peel. Practice tees see more wash cycles than any other piece of the uniform (typically 2-3 washes per week through a season).

faqs.q: How should we wash the Custom Basketball Practice T-Shirts?
faqs.a: Wash inside-out in cold water (warm or hot accelerates fabric thinning on lightweight polyester). Tumble dry low or hang dry — high heat shortens the fabric's structural life. Skip fabric softener; it leaves a residue that reduces moisture-wicking performance over time. Bleach is fine on whites but will gradually break down sublimated colors on darks, so spot-treat stains rather than full-load bleaching. Equipment managers running a 30-roster program through 2-3 weekly wash cycles get the longest fabric life with these settings — same care as competitive sublimated practice gear.

faqs.q: How does the mesh polyester fabric compare to a cotton practice tee in feel and breathability?
faqs.a: The performance polyester mesh is more breathable than cotton. It feels lighter and slicker, closer to a running shirt than a lifestyle tee. Cotton holds moisture and gets heavy through a long practice; the mesh polyester pulls sweat away from the skin. For gym sessions, conditioning runs, and indoor practice, we recommend the polyester.

faqs.q: How does the sublimated graphic handle shoulder-pad contact?
faqs.a: Sublimation bonds the design directly into the polyester fibers, so the graphic is part of the fabric, not a layer on top. The pad-contact zones (shoulder caps, upper chest, upper back) see the most wear, and on a sublimated jersey the color is dyed into the fabric, so there is no print layer to crack or peel at the contact points the way you'd see on a screen-printed jersey. The fabric itself will eventually thin in the high-contact zones. We recommend cold-water inside-out wash and tumble-dry low to maximize the fabric's structural life.

faqs.q: What's the right decoration method for jersey numbers — sublimated, tackle-twill, or embroidered? Which lasts longest?
faqs.a: Each method has a different look on a tackle-football jersey: Sublimated numbers are part of the fabric, so there is no print layer to crack or peel, but they sit flat on the fabric (no dimensional depth). Tackle-twill numbers are sewn-on twill panels with that classic varsity-program dimensional look. Embroidered numbers are crisp and dimensional, a good fit for small chest numbers. For example: tackle twill for the front and back numbers (classic look), embroidery for player names above the back number, and sublimation for the body color and sleeve stripes. You can also choose all tackle twill for the heritage look. Our design team will recommend the right method-and-element pairing for your team's design before production.

faqs.q: How do home and away uniforms coordinate — same design, contrast colors, or completely different look?
faqs.a: You can run your home and away uniforms as a coordinated pair: same design template, same logo treatments, same font, with inverted or contrast colors so opposing crews can tell which jersey is which from across the field. For example: home uniform has the team's primary color body with secondary-color numbers; away uniform inverts to a white/light body with primary-color numbers. You can also go fully different (for example, a throwback away uniform with different sleeve stripes). Tell us what you're going for at design submission and our design team will lay out the away mockup alongside your home set so you can see them side-by-side.

faqs.q: Can I order home and away uniforms in the same order?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend it: your whole order is made in the same dye batch, so the colors match across both sets. Ordering home and away in separate orders 6 months apart can introduce slight dye-lot variation between sets that's noticeable when both rotations are on the field for media day or yearbook photos. faqs.q: What do NFHS rules say about away-uniform colors?
faqs.a: Under the 2026 NFHS football rules, the visiting team wears jerseys with a white body and the home team wears a dark color that clearly contrasts with white. Numbers must be at least 8 inches tall on the front and 10 inches on the back (border included), with the body of each number in one solid color that clearly contrasts with the jersey. Your state association may add its own rules. Send them with your quote and your designer sets the numbers to fit. HAMLO SPORTS doesn't certify uniforms; your AD or coach files the league paperwork. Source: NFHS rules for home and visiting jerseys (June 2026), checked November 2026.

faqs.q: Reversible vs solid practice jerseys — which should I order for our program?

faqs.q: How is the practice jersey built for daily training?

faqs.q: How should we wash these to make them last? Daily wash through summer camp survives okay?
faqs.a: Wash inside-out in cold water (warm or hot accelerates mesh thinning on lightweight practice fabric). Tumble dry low or hang dry — high heat shortens the fabric's structural life. Skip fabric softener; it leaves a residue that reduces moisture-wicking performance over time. Through summer camp where jerseys see 1-2 wash cycles per day for 2 weeks straight, expect the mesh to start showing texture wear by the end of camp — that's normal and not a defect. Equipment managers running heavy daily-wash programs usually order an extra 25% beyond roster size so jerseys can rotate out of the wash cycle for a recovery day every few uses, which extends fabric life.

faqs.q: Quarter zip vs pullover hoodie vs full-zip hoodie — which should our staff and program order?

The QUARTER ZIP PULLOVER is the polished coaching/staff piece: raised collar reads sharp on camera, in the press box, and on recruiting visits; lightweight 100% polyester wears year-round without bulk; quarter-length zipper gives ventilation control without the casual look of a hoodie. The PULLOVER HOODIE is the warmer cold-weather bench piece: heavier weight, kangaroo pocket, hood for late-season cold and wet weather. The FULL-ZIP HOODIE is the sideline access piece: easy on and off for staff in headsets, with two zippered side pockets and a zip you can open part way. faqs.q: Why raised collar instead of a crew neck on the Custom Football Quarter Zip Pullover?
faqs.a: The raised collar is the design feature that lets the Custom Football Quarter Zip Pullover read as a coaching/staff piece rather than a casual sweatshirt. Camera-facing roles (head coach, athletic director, recruiting staff) get a clean neckline on game broadcasts, in press conferences, and on official program photos that a crew-neck sweatshirt can't deliver. The quarter-length zipper sits at the throat — close it for cold-weather formality and warmth retention, partially unzip for warm-weather ventilation, or fully open for a relaxed collar drape. The collar also gives the chest crest panel (typically embroidered school logo + sponsor mark) a defined frame that lifts the printed/embroidered graphics visually.

faqs.q: Can the Custom Football Quarter Zip Pullover be worn as a standalone sideline layer or only under a sideline jacket?

STANDALONE: warm-weather (60s-70s) practice and pregame, indoor staff wear, recruiting visits, post-game press, and travel days. AS A MID-LAYER under a sideline jacket: cool-weather games (40s-50s) where the jacket handles wind/rain and the quarter zip handles warmth retention. UNDER A WINDBREAKER: cold-and-windy late-season games where the quarter zip is a light insulating layer that fits trim under a shell. The lightweight 100% polyester construction means it doesn't add bulk under outer layers, and the raised collar still shows through an open jacket front, keeping the staff look consistent regardless of weather.

faqs.q: Is the Custom Football Windbreaker water-resistant or waterproof — what conditions does it handle?
faqs.a: The Custom Football Windbreaker is water-RESISTANT, not waterproof, an important distinction. It sheds wind and light rain (drizzle, passing showers, a wet sideline). It is NOT a sealed-seam waterproof rain shell for standing in a downpour for two hours; under sustained heavy rain it will eventually wet through at the seams. For most Friday-night sideline conditions (wind chill, intermittent rain, damp turf), it does exactly the job it's designed for: blocks the wind (the bigger comfort factor) and keeps light rain off. For full-downpour games, layer it over a hoodie and pair with the sideline cape for the players who'll be exposed longest.

faqs.q: What counts as a "two-tone" design on the Custom Ice Hockey Two-Tone Jerseys?
faqs.a: A two-tone hockey jersey carries two distinct color zones with a sharp visible boundary between them, in contrast to a traditional single-color jersey with trim stripes. Common two-tone placements include: contrasting shoulder yoke (one color across the shoulders and upper chest, second color on the body), sleeve-vs-body split (sleeves in one color, torso in another), vertical front split (left-and-right halves in different colors, often called a "harlequin" or "split" jersey), and chest-band split (horizontal band across the chest in a contrasting color). The boundary is built into the sublimation file (not stitched on as separate fabric panels). We'll show the boundary placement in the mockup before production starts.

faqs.q: Does a two-tone jersey count as a contrasting away jersey?

If you're using the two-tone as your away jersey, choose color blocking where the dominant body color contrasts with the home team's primary color — we'll flag any borderline contrast in the mockup review. For strict home/away contrast, our Custom Ice Hockey Game Day Away Jerseys ship in a single dominant away colorway.

faqs.q: Does the away uniform have to be a contrasting color from the home uniform?
faqs.a: Yes — visiting teams wear a uniform of contrasting color from the home team for officiating visibility. The traditional convention is light home (white-base jerseys with team-color trim and white-base socks with team-color stripes) and dark away (team-color base jerseys with white trim and dark-base socks with team-color stripes), so a team's away set is typically the darker, more saturated colorway across both the jersey and the matching socks. We design the away jersey + sock combination to read instantly from the bench, the back boards, and the top rows — strong base color, high-contrast nameplate, and high-contrast back number.

faqs.q: If I order both home and away uniform sets, will the team colors match exactly across all four pieces?
faqs.a: Yes. When home and away uniform sets are ordered together as a single purchase, all four pieces (home jersey + home sock + away jersey + away sock) are sublimated in the same dye batch on the same polyester base, so the team color matches across the home set and the away set. The home set's team-color accents (trim, sleeve stripes, sock striping) will match the away set's team-color base, and vice versa. If home and away sets are ordered separately months apart, dye lots can shift slightly between runs. For the cleanest home and away color match, order all four pieces together.

faqs.q: What is a hockey shell and how do teams use it?
faqs.a: A hockey shell (also called a practice pinnie or practice jersey shell) is a lightweight open-mesh pull-over worn over the shoulder pads during practice. A coach hands out two or three shell colors to split the roster into lines or teams for drills, scrimmages, and station work, so players can tell at a glance who's on which side. It pulls on and off over full shoulder pads, so teams can swap colors between drills without removing gear. It is not a game jersey. It has no fight strap and no tailored cut for pads; it's an oversized mesh layer for sorting groups at practice. For game wear, see our Custom Ice Hockey Game Day Home and Away Jerseys.

faqs.q: When should I choose a quarter-zip over a full-zip hoodie, pullover hoodie, or crewneck for soccer warmups?
faqs.a: The quarter-zip is the warmup layer that adjusts mid-session: open the zip a couple of inches when body heat builds during dynamic stretches, close it again when wind comes off the pitch. A full-zip hoodie strips off completely in seconds (best for match-day warmups where the keeper needs the layer off the moment the whistle blows), the pullover hoodie keeps a closed front for the full warmup window (best for cold travel days and team photos), and the crewneck sweatshirt is the no-hood casual layer for off-pitch and bus rides.

faqs.q: What's the difference between the quarter-zip training top and a long-sleeve training shirt?
faqs.a: Both run on ~150 GSM moisture-wicking polyester, but the quarter-zip adds a 6 to 8 inch placket and stand-up collar that the long-sleeve training shirt doesn't have. The long-sleeve training shirt is the under-layer or warmer-weight session base. Players wear it through the full session at a constant temperature. The quarter-zip goes over the training shirt (or directly over a kit) for the pre-game and dynamic warmup window, where you actually need to vent heat without stopping to take a layer off. On cold training days, layer the quarter-zip on top of the long-sleeve training shirt.

faqs.q: How durable is the zipper and stand collar?
faqs.a: Care: cold wash gentle cycle, zip closed before washing to protect the teeth, inside-out helps the sublimation print, air-dry or low-heat tumble. Avoid high-heat drying because that's what shortens both the zipper slider life and the stand-collar memory.

faqs.q: What do softball uniform rules say about sleeveless jerseys?
faqs.a: High school softball follows the NFHS Softball Uniforms guide (checked Oct 31, 2026). Every team member's uniform must be the same color and style, but sleeve length may vary from player to player, as long as each player's sleeves are about the same length and not ragged, frayed or slit. NFHS also requires a number on the back of every jersey, at least 6 inches high, in a solid color that contrasts with the shirt. Travel, college and adult leagues set their own rules, so check your rulebook and tell us the rule on your quote. Pair with softball standard pants or standard knickers for the complete uniform.

faqs.q: Why does double-knee reinforcement matter on a softball pant?
faqs.a: The knee panel takes the most punishment on a softball pant. A single-layer pant wears through at the knee first — that's where you see fraying, thinning, and eventually holes before the rest of the pant shows any wear. Double-knee reinforcement adds a second layer of the 220 GSM performance polyester shell across the knee panel , roughly doubling the abrasion resistance exactly where the pant needs it most. It is built into the pant construction, not an add-on, and there is no upcharge for it.

Second, programs that want one bottom for everything : the drawstring pant works as a warm-up pant and a game pant, so a program does not need a separate warm-up bottom. Third, quick changes : at tournaments with tight turnarounds between games, pull-on pants save time. The trade-off is purely about looks: the belted standard pant gives the more traditional, dialed-in varsity look, while the drawstring pant reads slightly more casual. Both are the same 220 GSM performance polyester shell, same double-knee reinforcement, same durability; the choice is whether the program values pull-on convenience or the belted traditional look.

faqs.q: Is the windbreaker a warmth layer, and how water-resistant is it really?
faqs.a: The windbreaker is a wind-and-light-rain shell, not a warmth layer . That is the most important thing to understand before ordering. The water-resistant polyester shell blocks wind and sheds light rain and drizzle, and it has a breathable mesh lining. But it has no fleece insulation, so on a genuinely cold morning it is worn OVER a fleece layer (a crewneck, hoodie, or quarter-zip), not instead of one. On water-resistance specifically: it is water-resistant, not fully waterproof . It will keep a player dry through a passing shower, drizzle, or wind-driven mist, and the shell sheds light rain, but a sustained downpour will eventually soak through, because a truly waterproof seam-sealed rain shell is a different (and much pricier) garment. For softball's typical use (wind on open fields, cool mornings, the occasional light shower), the windbreaker is the right call. If your program plays through heavy rain regularly, layer the windbreaker over a fleece and keep a dry change in the bag.

That makes the windbreaker one of the most design-flexible layers we offer: an all-over team print is on the table here in a way it is not on the cotton-fleece crewneck and hoodies. Embroidery (a compact left-chest crest) and screen printing (opaque logos) are also available. The one method we do NOT use on the windbreaker is tackle twill . faqs.q: How does the 4-way stretch handle the full motion range volleyball demands?
faqs.a: Volleyball asks the jersey to do four conflicting things at once: stretch overhead for serves and attacks, compress to the body for passing, breathe through long sets in hot gyms, and stay still on the torso during dives and defensive digs. The ~160 GSM polyester knit with 4-way stretch handles all four. The 4-way stretch means the fabric extends and recovers along BOTH the horizontal and vertical axes — when a player reaches overhead for an attack, the sleeves stretch lengthwise without binding at the shoulder; when they dive forward for a defensive dig, the torso fabric stretches sideways without pulling tight across the chest. Moisture-wicking finish pulls sweat away from the skin and pushes it to the fabric surface where it evaporates, keeping players cool through tournament rounds and back-to-back matches. The full-length sleeve adds the arm coverage without the warmth penalty of cotton — polyester knit is the right fabric for indoor volleyball.

faqs.q: Racerback vs sleeveless vs cap-sleeve vs short-sleeve — which volleyball jersey cut fits each player?
faqs.a: Four different jersey cuts for four different player preferences. A crewneck stays flat at the collar so the headgear seats correctly. Second, layering: when the program runs the warmup jacket over the sideline top for a coordinated tournament look, the crewneck disappears cleanly under the jacket collar, while a hood bunches up and breaks the line. Third, warmth: a full-zip leaves a thin gap and seam down the chest where cold gets in, while the solid pullover front retains warmth through cold-gym practices and recovery sessions. faqs.q: Quarter-zip, full-zip, or lightweight track jacket — which wrestling warmup layer should I order?

The full-zip warmup jacket opens all the way down for quick on-off over headgear and singlet between matches. The lightweight track jacket is a thinner full-zip for travel and warm-venue wear. faqs.q: Why does the quarter-zip warmup jacket stay on during stretching and shadow drilling?

A full-zip jacket pops or gaps open during the same movements. The raglan sleeve construction gives a clean overhead reach. When you heat up between rounds, drop the collar zip to vent without taking the jacket off.

faqs.a: No minimum order. Order a single pair for one wrestler or outfit the entire roster; the process is the same either way. Per-pant pricing goes as low as $39.99 on orders of 101 or more. Design and color setup are included in the per-pant price, with no per-color charge on sublimated designs.

faqs.q: How long does production take, and do I see a design first?
faqs.a: You get a free design mockup within 12 hours of sending us your logo and colors, with unlimited revisions until you approve it. Production takes 2 to 3 weeks after you approve your design; shipping to your door then takes 3 to 5 days. Need it sooner? Ask for a free rush. We do it when production allows, and it is never guaranteed.

faqs.q: What sizes do the warmup jogger pants come in?
faqs.a: Pants are available from Youth YS through Adult 4XL at the same per-piece price with no upcharge at either end, so the same matched team look fits youth-club wrestlers through heavyweight adults on one roster. Size each wrestler from the chart in the Size Guide on this page. For help with the tapered fit or length, ask us.
